title: K7 Conformance Verdict
description: The sole durable output of a K7 review. Written by the audit subprocess, never by the builder. Validated by the commit hook against HEAD before any commit is permitted.

concept.description: Concept name, matching the S3 anchor.

round.description: Unbounded. The old RD-9 cap of 2 was a patch for a loop caused by in-session review; subprocess separation removes the cause. Termination is now handled by `progress` below: a round that changes nothing must HALT.

progress.description: Null on round 1. Otherwise the runner computes this by diffing against the prior verdict. A mechanical verdict is a function of the tree, so an unchanged tree with an unchanged failing set means the loop is not converging.

changed.description: False when tree_sha and the failing-check set both match the prior round.

tree_sha.description: git rev-parse HEAD^{tree} at review time. The commit hook compares this to the current tree; a mismatch means the verdict is stale and the commit is denied.

s3_anchor_tag.description: The frozen S3 tag this review was conducted against, e.g. s3-anchor-v1.0.

modules.description: Modules in scope for this round.

kind.description: RD-32 (2.7.0): the foundation checkpoint, the final review, or any other round (a re-check, an owner-ordered round). A verdict from before RD-32 has none.

facets.description: The final review's passes (RD-32): one per facet, each reviewing its modules in full, then one across the seams.

scope.description: Credited review (tools/manifests.py): each module's content fingerprint and the mode the runner gave it. Written by the runner; a verdict from before credited review has none.

mode.description: checkpoint (RD-32): reviewed whole for correctness only (CC-1, CC-2, CC-4); credits nothing and is no full review.

manifest.description: sha256 of the module's canonical manifest.

base.description: diff mode: the reviewed commit of the newest concluded round that had the module in scope.

credit_round.description: credited mode: the concluded round whose scope held this fingerprint.

unresolved.description: Internal imports the runner could not resolve; a module with any is never credited.

invocation.description: Only a separate process may produce a verdict. An in-session subagent cannot satisfy this field honestly, which is the point.

builder_transcript_seen.description: Asserted by the runner script, not by the reviewer. The runner controls the prompt and therefore knows.

worktree_clean_after.description: The reviewer must leave the tree byte-identical. A dirty exit invalidates the verdict.

checks.description: One entry per conformance check. Keys are check IDs (CC-1..CC-7 for K7).

mechanical.description: True only if the result came from a command exit code. Makes the prose/mechanical ratio countable, so policy can require a minimum.

rationale.description: Required when mechanical is false. Prose judgment must be labelled as such.

basis.description: A bare number is rejected. Each deduction must name a check and a specific finding, so the score is reconstructable rather than asserted.

blocking.description: Required non-empty when verdict is RETURN or HALT.

next_action.description: Single imperative sentence. Copied verbatim into STATE.md by the runner.

proposed_tests.description: Amendment S-1 (the frozen test set). A further test for a guard element the frozen set already covers: a proposal, never a blocking item, which the runner appends to INSTRUMENTS/test-intake-log.md for the end-of-stretch dedupe. A guard element the frozen set does not cover is not a proposal: it is a CC-4 failure, and goes in blocking. Optional; a verdict from before the rule has none.

guard_element.description: The guard element the test claims to cover in that module: the Outcome of S3 §5, or the invariant a row with no named outcome guards.

test.description: The forbidden input and the expected rejection.

why.description: What the frozen set's row for that element misses.

allOf.description: A RETURN says fix these and come back, so it must name them.

A HALT carries exactly one entry: the halt-class constraint breached. Offering a fix list alongside a HALT converts it back into a defect queue, which is the failure the verdict exists to prevent — so the schema makes that unrepresentable.
No-progress stop, replacing the old round cap. A round that changed neither the tree nor the failing set cannot report anything but HALT.

then.description: A PASS is impossible while structure violations stand.
